text:
ana: Quick question — we need to settle on fallthrough semantics for latency-tiered routes when the exact model variant is unavailable (quantized vs fp16, region mismatch). Thinking about the runtime contract and what callers should expect.
ryan: tl;dr: prefer same-tenant compatible variant, then region-preferral, then cost-tier. But need clear signal back to the client so apps can downgrade gracefully.
kai: +1 to explicit signal. also: what about cached KV states? falling back to different variant may break cache hits and perf assumptions.
marta: We also need to consider billing implications — if we autoswitch to a cheaper variant we still might want to bill at requested model's deduped rate or at the served model rate? ops/legal will care.
nana (ana): @ryan by "signal" you mean an explicit field in response metadata like `served_model` + `fallthrough_reason`?
ryan: exactly. e.g., response metadata: { served_model: "gptx-8q", requested_model: "gptx-8f", fallthrough_reason: "region_unavailable" } — short and machine-readable.
kai: let's also include an opaque `compat_level` or `quality_score` so downstream can decide to re-try or degrade features.
marta: For backwards compatibility, default behavior should be to preserve previous semantics (most callers expect fallback without error). But flag a runtime-config to opt-in to strict-mode that errors instead of falling through.
nana (ana): proposal sketch for policy config (very rough):
```
route: {
  priority: [latency, cost],
  fallthrough: [compatible_variant, region_fallback, cost_variant],
  strict: false
}
```
ryan: Implementation notes: the policy evaluator should expose a deterministic ordering and a small, stable enum of reasons ("compat_mismatch", "region_down", "capacity_preempt"). Avoid freeform strings.
kai: Also add telemetry hooks: increment counters per reason and per tenant. We need histograms of downstream latency delta when fallback happens.
marta: migration plan: start with a sim run that logs what would have happened, then a canary that actually performs fallthroughs but with a header `X-Fallthrough-Logged-Only: true` so clients see metadata but responses still prefer requested model when possible.
ajamie-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for policy change on shard us-west-2 at 2026-04-02T09:00Z.
nana (ana): Tests: unit for policy ordering, integration with runtime (simulate capacity loss + quantized mismatch), e2e sim against production traces for 48h. Add a small eval set to verify output quality delta <= 3% for promoted fallthrough variants.
ryan: We should also codify an API version bump for the `meta` block so SDKs can opt into reading `fallthrough_reason` — don't silently change shape.
kai: Edge case: chained fallthroughs across adapters (e.g., region fallback -> cheaper quantized variant). We need to avoid infinite loops and prefer a single-pass evaluation with max steps.
marta: Ops: record both token burn and billing model; attach `billing_model` to metadata.
nana (ana): Next steps I propose: 1) write a short RFC with policy enum + metadata schema, 2) add sim harness change, 3) telemetry dashboard, 4) canary. I'll draft RFC and ping y'all.
ryan: sounds good. I can help with the telemetry bits.
kai: I'll prototype evaluator change and add max-step guard.
marta: I'll check with finance about billing semantics and file a ticket.
nana (ana): thanks — will drop RFC link here when ready. :rocket:
